We need to fix compilation errors. The test class uses many imports that are missing. We need to add import statements for JUnit 5 annotations, Mockito, Jackson, java.util, reflection, etc., and also import the classes from com.networknt.schema like JsonSchema, PropertiesValidator, ValidationContext, etc.

Also need to resolve the inner class MutatingValidator extends PropertiesValidator: need to import PropertiesValidator.

Also need to fix the stub that tries to access getValidator() inside StubJsonSchema (in concurrent modification test) – they used getValidator() which doesn't exist. Actually they want to get reference to validator. In original code maybe they used a method to get validator reference? Not sure. In test they attempt to set a field "this$0" via reflection on StubJsonSchema class, which is an inner class of test, not of validator, so that doesn't make sense. Actually they want to set a field inside stub to reference the validator. The stub class is static, so no outer reference. They attempt to get field "this$0" which would be synthetic for non-static inner class. Since StubJsonSchema is static, there is no this$0. So this will fail compile because they reference getValidator() method not defined. In the test code they call mutating.preloadJsonSchema() which inside overrides to add entry to validator's map. But they need reference to validator. They attempted to set via reflection: Field validatorField = PropertiesValidator_preloadJsonSchema_Test.StubJsonSchema.class.getDeclaredField("this$0"); That's not correct. Instead we can modify the test to give StubJsonSchema a reference to validator via a field.

Simplify: we can change the test to avoid reflection hack. Provide a custom StubJsonSchema subclass that holds a reference to validator set via constructor.

Implement in test: create a new class extends StubJsonSchema with a validator field.

But we cannot change test behavior drastically; we can adjust code to compile.

Simpler: add a method getValidator() to StubJsonSchema returning a ValidationContext? Not.

Better: modify the concurrentModificationDuringPreload test to create an anonymous StubJsonSchema that overrides preloadJsonSchema and uses a static variable referencing validator.

We can add a static field in test class: static PropertiesValidator currentValidator; then set before test. Then inside stub's preloadJsonSchema, refer to currentValidator.

Add static field: private static PropertiesValidator concurrentValidator; Then in test, after creating validator, set concurrentValidator = validator; Then stub can use that.

Modify the test code accordingly.

Also need to import necessary classes: org.junit.jupiter.api.*, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith, org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension, org.mockito.Mock, org.mockito.Mockito.*, org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor, static imports for assertions.

Add imports for java.util.*, java.lang.reflect.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode, com.networknt.schema.* (JsonSchema, ValidationContext, PropertiesValidator, JsonSchemaVisitor, SchemaType, FormatValidator, ValidatorTypeCode, SpecVersion). We can import whole package.

Also need to import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentModificationException.

Also need to import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.* maybe.

Add necessary static imports for when, any, anyString, mock, clearInvocations, verify, times.

Also need to import java.util.ArrayList, LinkedHashMap, Collections.

Now adjust code: Add imports at top.

Add static field for concurrent test.

Modify concurrentModificationDuringPreload test:

Replace reflection part with setting static field.

Implementation:

Add static PropertiesValidator concurrentValidator; at class level.

In test method:

replaceSchemasMap(validator, map);
concurrentValidator = validator;
assertThrows(ConcurrentModificationException.class, validator::preloadJsonSchema);
concurrentValidator = null; // optional

In StubJsonSchema mutating = new StubJsonSchema() { @Override public void preloadJsonSchema() { concurrentValidator.getSchemas().put("new", new StubJsonSchema()); } };

Need to ensure getSchemas() method exists in PropertiesValidator (public). According to dependent info, there is getSchemas().

Now compile.
